measurement_basis: pushed Control implementation with focused regression verification

observation.source_interface: MNCS Control GitService branch APIs and MCP tool descriptions

outcome.implementation_change: Control now rejects refs/... values at branch creation, checkout, merge, push, pull, and worktree branch boundaries. Tool descriptions state that branch arguments use short names. This prevents the reproduced fully qualified-looking input from reaching Git through those APIs.
outcome.effectiveness_assessment: input-boundary regression verified; subsequent agent use and reduction in ref failures not yet observed
outcome.analysis_limit: The bounded Git fixture shows that refs/heads/main as an input causes the exact ambiguity, while main succeeds on the current Git version. The historical command/error pairing remains unresolved; this implementation prevents the qualified input but does not establish the cause of that earlier recorded operation.

related_work.campaign_objective: Improve MNCS's ability to observe, interpret, and improve how the environment serves agents working within MNCS.
related_work.work_intent_goal: Improve MNCS's ability to observe, interpret, and improve how the environment serves agents working within MNCS.

improvement_relation.basis: Control's public branch operations previously passed refs/... strings through to Git. A controlled local bare-remote fixture reproduced the ambiguous refspec when refs/heads/main was passed, and a committed regression test verifies that all branch-oriented API boundaries now reject the prefix before Git is invoked.
improvement_relation.effectiveness_assessment: implementation and immediate input-boundary behavior verified; future recurrence and agent discoverability not assessed
not_measured: whether future agents avoid namespace-prefixed branch arguments
whether this prevents a recurrence in live Git operations
whether other reported push or merge failures share this cause
longitudinal reduction in ambiguous ref operations
agent success rate for Git operations across different models
the root cause of historical authorization failures unrelated to this controlled ref case
